The main takeaway from our work is that

the cell penetrating peptide can be successfully used to increase the cellular uptake of polymer conjugates and the internalization efficacy depends on both the type of the cell penetrating peptide and the length of the spacer between the peptide and the polymer backbone.
polymer–peptide carriers can be designed to improve the cellular uptake of a drug cargo, but this improvement depends on the type of peptide, its length and the length of the spacer.
the internalization efficacy of the studied CPP–polymer carriers depends on the peptide type and spacer length.
